newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MTBE rises on plant turnaround talk, demand.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MTBE rises on plant turnaround talk, demand.

text.p: U.S. spot MTBE prices rose for the third consecutive week as barrels for prompt supply dried up amid news of plant turnarounds and octane demand, players said on Monday.
The about two-cent rise began on Thursday ahead of the three-day Fourth of July weekend, with the strength staying through to what was quiet activity on Monday.
In the East Coast, New York Harbor prompt MTBE was up about two cents to 91.00/91.50 cents. A 20,000-barrel parcel for any July delivery traded hands Monday for 90.00 cents.

In the U.S. Gulf Coast, prompt MTBE was notional due to the few barrels available since supply was tightened by plant turnarounds and shutdowns in May. Traders said a prompt barrel would probably sell for a $1.00 if it could be found.
Any month barrels were pegged 0.75 cent higher at between 87.50 cents and 88.00 cents a gallon, traders said.

Part of the increase was due to talk Belvieu Environmental Fuels will shut down its 12,000 to 15,000 barrel-per-day MTBE plant for a turnaround this weekend instead of in August, as previously planned, traders said.
In addition, demand for MTBE as an octane enhancer has increased with the recent strong pricing of toulene, a competitve octane booster now trading for about 92.00 cents a gallon.
"MTBE will be the octane of choice until it too reaches into the 90s," said a USG trader.
-- Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk 1212 859-1631--
